rationale: This is a moderator-stacking variant of the archive's existing "Serial dilution with near-term debt overhang," and the claimed orthogonality is false — dlc/act and wcap/at are mechanically overlapping short-term liquidity constructs (dlc sits inside lct, wcap = act − lct), so the test mostly re-weights the same conditioning information.

target_name: Funding gap facing a refinancing deadline
rationale: A defensible diagnosis-driven pairing of the signed issuance-minus-cash-flow leg (large alpha, no slope) with the maturity-deadline moderator (large slope), though it remains an incremental leg×moderator recombination within a heavily mined family.

Conditioning payout on maturity timing is a genuinely untested and economically coherent channel here, but the negative expected sign fights the well-documented positive payout/dividend-level premium, so the level leg may simply proxy mature high-quality firms and the interaction may load on size and industry.

target_name: Continuous refinancing with a short maturity ladder
rationale: Three-year cumulative debt issuance scaled by assets is close to the published debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly, and multiplying it by another debt-burden ratio makes the "interaction" largely a leverage double-count rather than a state-contingent test, limiting its value beyond the decomposition diagnostic.

target_name: Internal funding surplus with stable scaling
rationale: The repaired leg is essentially cash-flow profitability minus net external financing — two separately published anomalies bundled together — and two prior self-sufficiency tests in this archive delivered significant results in the direction opposite the stated positive sign, so the sign prior is contradicted rather than merely mismeasured.
Swapping RANK for IND_RANK on one leg of an already-evaluated signal is precisely the cosmetic single-operator variant the objective warns against, and it offers no new economic mechanism.
